title: Hard Eligibility Before Optimization
summary: Job-to-Node evaluates hard eligibility before optimization, while Generalized Compute Intentions may only plan over the resulting authoritative evidence.
why: A cheap, fast or idle resource is irrelevant if policy, jurisdiction, runtime, capability or mandatory resource requirements reject it.
invariants: Hard eligibility is evaluated before optimisation.
A semantic planner may explain a veto but cannot override it.
Telemetry and economic ranking cannot turn an ineligible candidate into an eligible one.
evidence_note: Grounded in Job-to-Node v0.6/network6 hard-eligibility semantics and Generalized Compute Intentions v0.1-dev5 authority tests.
